newsitem.title: GERMANY: Supreme court upholds German election law.
newsitem.headline: Supreme court upholds German election law.

text.p: Germany's supreme court on Thursday upheld voting laws that assured Chancellor Helmut Kohl a workable majority in parliament.
The court said the so-called "overhang mandates" that gave Kohl a 10-seat majority did not discriminate against any party.
The court also upheld a complex law concerning small parties that allowed eastern German reform communists to be returned to parliament at the last general election in 1994.

The decision means Germany's current election laws, which boosted Kohl's majority from two to 10 due to "overhand mandates" for which seats had to be added after the vote, will not be changed for the 1998 election.
Kohl's current majority would not have been endangered if the court had found the law unconstitutional, but such a ruling would have had hard-to-foresee effects for the next vote.
